newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Algerian to be UN-OAU Central Africa envoy.
newsitem.headline: Algerian to be UN-OAU Central Africa envoy.

text.p: Algerian diplomat Mohamed Sahnoun, who once headed the U.N. operation in Somalia, will be named a special representative for the troubled Great Lakes region of Central Africa, diplomats said on Tuesday.
They said he would jointly represent both the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity (OAU).

Sahnoun was appointed to the U.N. Somalia post in April 1992 but resigned the following October after a row with then-Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, who was succeeded on January 1 by Kofi Annan of Ghana.
Sahnoun was rebuked by Boutros-Ghali for publicly saying the United Nations came too late to save many of the millions of Somalis facing starvation.
Sahnoun's departure was widely lamented by aid organisations at the time.
His diplomatic career has included service as Algeria's ambassador to the United Nations in 1982-84, the United States (1984-89), France (1979-1982) and Germany (1975-79).
Sahnoun was a deputy secretary-general of the Arab League in 1973 and from 1964 to 1973 was deputy secretary-general of the OAU.
The Great Lakes region of Central Africa has been in turmoil for the past three years following large-scale ethnic violence between Hutus and Tutsis in Rwanda and Burundi.

Genocidal massacres in Rwanda in 1994 took the lives of between 500,000 and a million Tutsis and moderate Hutus. This was followed by the flight of hundreds of thousands of refugees into Zaire and other neighbouring countries, including Tanzania and Uganda.
The refugees included many Rwandan Hutus who feared retribution after Tutsis wrested power from Hutu hardliners. Many have still not returned home.
The situation has been further complicated by fighting that erupted late last year in eastern Zaire between government troops and Tutsi-led rebels.
